case_text:
Vignette:
A 2-month-old male infant is brought in by his parents who are concerned about yellowish, greasy-appearing scales on the baby's scalp that have been present for approximately 2 weeks. The scales are thick in some areas. The parents report the baby is feeding well, gaining weight appropriately, and sleeping normally. There is no rash elsewhere on the body. On examination, there are adherent yellowish-white greasy scales over the anterior fontanelle and vertex of the scalp. There is no underlying erythema, no oozing, and no involvement of the face or diaper area. The infant is content and thriving.
